definitions.explanation: Clothing designed for manual labor or physical work. Includes uniforms worn at factories, construction sites, and other workplaces where durability and practicality are important.

examples.japanese: {作業服|さぎょうふく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{着替|きが}えた→着替える：04603_kigaeru⟧。
examples.english: I changed into my work clothes.

examples.japanese: ⟦{工場|こうじょう}→工場：01082_koujou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{全員|ぜんいん}→全員：03310_zenin⟧{作業服|さぎょうふく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{着|き}→着る：00541_kiru⟧⟦なければならない→なければならない：27600_nakerebanaranai⟧。
examples.english: Everyone at the factory must wear work uniforms.

examples.japanese: ⟦{汚|よご}れた→汚れる：01293_yogoreru⟧{作業服|さぎょうふく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{洗濯機|せんたくき}→洗濯機：04969_sentakuki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|い}れて→入れる：01098_ireru⟧、⟦シャワー→シャワー：04503_shawaa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{浴|あ}びた→浴びる：02844_abiru⟧。
examples.english: I put my dirty work clothes in the washing machine and took a shower.

notes:
USAGE:
In Japan, many companies provide {作業服|さぎょうふく} to employees working in manufacturing, construction, and similar fields. The term also applies to the distinctive blue or gray uniforms commonly seen at Japanese factories.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {作業服|さぎょうふく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{着|き}る→着る：00541_kiru⟧ (to wear work clothes)
- {作業服|さぎょうふく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{着替|きが}える→着替える：04603_kigaeru⟧ (to change into work clothes)
- {作業服|さぎょうふく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧まま (still in one's work clothes)
